question: Does decaying the periodic auxiliary objective prevent its late-horizon regression without sacrificing held-out causal-LM loss?
prior_result: hf_periodic_gpt2_pride_full_corpus_256step_20260823.json remains ready_but_negative and is not pooled with this study.

generation.decoding: greedy, natural EOS, no inference intervention
generation.scope: Prior frozen prompts are reused. Milestones are descriptive, never checkpoint selection. Inspect continuation text and generated lengths alongside loop scores; shorter output alone is not improved language quality.

acceptance.mechanism: Every treatment run must have nonzero periodic candidates and finite losses; policy and final absolute slot must match.

boundaries: Single-factor treatment: same candidate planner, active-position normalization, base strength and training settings; only the decay schedule changes between treatment arms.
CPU float32 throughout; no GPU speed claim and no historical MPS result pooling.

Batch size one avoids partial-batch label-count imbalance; preflight checks every collated train/eval row has exactly 127 shifted labels. Accumulation is sixteen, including HF's smaller final epoch group.

All selected validation blocks are evaluated, not the two-block development smoke subset. Corpus rows are split with the same seed across arms; this is a same-book held-out split, not cross-book generalization.
Run order rotates across seeds. No early stopping, checkpoint selection or post-outcome retuning. No automatic restart into an existing output directory.
Prespecified seeds are distinct from the preceding 109/113/127 study and development seed 7. This is a small paired experiment, not statistical significance or general Z-space superiority.
Retain full raw artifacts locally; publish all conditions, derived results, hashes and reproduction instructions without private paths or model weights.
